guideTitle: The Best Reclining Gaming Chairs, from Console Recliners to Flat-Back Models
metaDescription: Reclining gaming chairs range from wheel-free console recliners to 180-degree flat-back models. We compared eight on recline range, footrest, capacity, massage and warranty.
introParagraphs: "Recliner" covers several quite different chairs. Some are desk-style gaming chairs whose backs tilt to 155 or even 180 degrees; others are console or home-theater recliners built to stay in one spot in front of a TV. Decide which you want before comparing angles.

Among the desk-style chairs, the maximum recline angle, the footrest and the weight rating are the main differences. A flat 180-degree recline is available at budget prices, but a deep recline is only useful if you have room behind the chair.
The eight chairs below range from about $78 to about $314 at the time of writing. Our comparison is based on published specifications and listed features, not hands-on testing.

respawn-900-console-recliner.summary: A wheel-free recliner with a separate footrest, 360-degree swivel, cup holder and five-year warranty.
respawn-900-console-recliner.description:
The RESPAWN 900 is a true console recliner: it has no wheels, so it stays put in front of a TV, but it still swivels 360 degrees. Its 135-degree recline and footrest operate independently.

A built-in cup holder and accessory pouch keep controllers and drinks within reach, it is rated for 275 lb, and it has a five-year warranty, tied for the longest here.

It was the most expensive chair here at the time of writing, and without wheels it won't roll to a desk.
cons: Most expensive here at the time of writing
respawn-900-console-recliner.bestFor: A fixed console or living-room gaming spot.
respawn-900-console-recliner.skipIf: You want to roll between a desk and a reclined position; the RESPAWN 110 Pro has wheels.

respawn-110-pro-recliner.summary: A wheeled chair with continuously adjustable recline to 155 degrees, multi-point footrest and five-year warranty.
respawn-110-pro-recliner.description:
The RESPAWN 110 Pro suits a desk that doubles as a place to lean back: RESPAWN describes a near-infinite recline to 155 degrees, so you can stop at any angle rather than a few fixed positions, and its footrest adjusts at multiple points.

It has two layers of thick foam, an adjustable headrest, a 275 lb rating and a five-year warranty, and it has the largest base of buyer feedback here.

It costs more than the budget recliners, and its buyer feedback is somewhat less positive than theirs.
cons: Less positive feedback than some cheaper chairs
respawn-110-pro-recliner.bestFor: Desk gaming with frequent reclining at different angles.
respawn-110-pro-recliner.skipIf: You want to lie completely flat; the Homall recliners reach 180 degrees.

homall-recliner-180.summary: A budget chair that reclines fully flat to 180 degrees, with a reinforced steel footrest.
homall-recliner-180.description:
The Homall recliner goes further than any RESPAWN here: from 90 degrees to fully flat at 180, at about $130 at the time of writing.

It has thick sponge padding, a reinforced steel footrest, wide curved armrests and four anti-scratch feet, and an extensive base of buyer feedback.

Its 265 lb rating is the lowest among the desk-style chairs, and a flat recline needs plenty of room behind the chair.
homall-recliner-180.bestFor: Lying flat between sessions on a budget.
homall-recliner-180.skipIf: You prefer PU leather; the Homall Leather model has the same recline for slightly less.

homall-recliner-leather-upgrade.summary: Homall's PU leather version of the 180-degree recliner, with a thicker footrest.
homall-recliner-leather-upgrade.description:
This Homall is the PU leather version of the flat-recline chair, with a dark home-theater look, the same 90- to 180-degree recline and a footrest Homall describes as thicker. It includes lumbar support and anti-scratch feet.

It was listed slightly below the fabric version at the time of writing and shares its 265 lb rating.

PU leather can feel warmer than fabric, and the two Homall listings share buyer feedback, so it's hard to separate them on that basis.
pros: Slightly cheaper than the fabric version
cons: Shares feedback with the fabric version
homall-recliner-leather-upgrade.bestFor: A home-theater look with a flat recline.
homall-recliner-leather-upgrade.skipIf: You run warm; the fabric Homall or GTPLAYER may be more comfortable.

yaheetech-recliner-massage-footrest.summary: The lowest-priced chair here, with USB massage lumbar, folding footrest and 300 lb rating.
yaheetech-recliner-massage-footrest.description:
The Yaheetech is the least expensive recliner here at the time of writing, and it adds a USB massage lumbar pillow and a folding footrest, with very positive buyer feedback.

It reclines to 135 degrees, has a detachable headrest, SGS-certified casters and a 300 lb rating.

Its 135-degree recline is well short of the Homall chairs' flat position.
cons: Less buyer feedback than the top sellers
yaheetech-recliner-massage-footrest.bestFor: A modest recline with massage on the smallest budget.
yaheetech-recliner-massage-footrest.skipIf: You want a deep recline; the Homall 180 costs about $50 more.

gtplayer-recliner-spring.summary: A pocket-spring cushion under breathable Leatheraire fabric, with armrests that move as you recline.
gtplayer-recliner-spring.description:
The GTPLAYER prioritizes seat feel: a pocket-spring cushion GTPLAYER compares to a sofa, under Leatheraire fabric it rates as twice as breathable as standard PU leather.

Its armrests adjust with you as you recline, it is rated for 300 lb and has a one-year warranty.

The listing doesn't state a maximum recline angle, and its warranty is far shorter than the RESPAWN chairs'.
gtplayer-recliner-spring.bestFor: A soft, breathable seat where deep recline is secondary.
gtplayer-recliner-spring.skipIf: Recline angle is the priority; the Homall 180 states its range.

sweetcrispy-massage-recliner.summary: A sofa-style recliner with 90- to 160-degree recline and 8 remote-controlled massage modes.
sweetcrispy-massage-recliner.description:
The Sweetcrispy looks like home-theater furniture rather than a gaming chair: a sofa-style recliner with a 90- to 160-degree range.

It has 8 massage modes with 2 vibration intensities on a remote, and Sweetcrispy quotes about 5 minutes of assembly. It is rated for 275 lb.

It isn't designed for desk use, and it has less buyer feedback than several chairs here.
sweetcrispy-massage-recliner.bestFor: A media room chair with massage.
sweetcrispy-massage-recliner.skipIf: You want a console recliner with swivel and storage; the RESPAWN 900 has both.

homall-big-tall-recliner-400.summary: A 400 lb-rated chair with 4D armrests, air-pump lumbar and 155-degree recline.
homall-big-tall-recliner-400.description:
The Homall Big & Tall is the only chair here rated above 300 lb, at 400 lb, and it pairs that with 4D armrests and an adjustable air-pump lumbar.

It reclines from 90 to 155 degrees, has a retractable footrest and uses a wingless, breathable backrest design.

It is a new listing with very little buyer feedback, and what exists is less positive than for the other chairs here, so read recent reviews before buying.
cons: Less positive feedback than others here
homall-big-tall-recliner-400.bestFor: Users who need more than a 300 lb rating in a reclining chair.
homall-big-tall-recliner-400.skipIf: You're well within 300 lb; the Yaheetech or GTPLAYER costs less or has more feedback.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Desk-style chairs roll and recline; console and home-theater recliners, like the RESPAWN 900 and Sweetcrispy, stay in one place.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Match the recline to your space
buyingCriteria.explanation: Maximum angles here range from 135 to 180 degrees. Deep recline needs clear space behind the chair.
Ratings run from 265 lb to 400 lb. Recline adds stress, so choose a rating with margin.
The RESPAWN chairs list five years; the GTPLAYER lists one.

faq.q: What's the difference between a gaming recliner and a regular gaming chair?
faq.a: Many gaming chairs tilt back; recliners here either reach deeper angles, up to 180 degrees, or use a console-style build with independent footrests and no wheels.
Both Homall 180 models. The RESPAWN 110 Pro reaches 155 degrees, the Sweetcrispy 160 and the RESPAWN 900 135.
No. The RESPAWN 900 skips wheels to stay put in front of a TV. Wheeled chairs are more practical at a desk.

faq.q: Is a big-and-tall recliner worth it if I'm under 300 lb?
faq.a: Only for its other features. The Homall Big & Tall's main advantage is its 400 lb rating, and it has little buyer feedback so far.
Here, mainly the RESPAWN chairs' five-year warranties and, for the 900, a console-style build with independent footrest, rather than more recline.

bottomLine: For a desk chair you'll recline in, the Homall 180 lies flat for a low price, and the RESPAWN 110 Pro adds finer angle control and a five-year warranty. The Yaheetech is the lowest-cost option with massage.
For a fixed spot in front of a TV, the RESPAWN 900 is the console recliner to consider, and the Sweetcrispy suits a home-theater look. The Homall Big & Tall is the choice above 300 lb.
